setup.zh: 十月初十，子时，药园。你蹲在下风口的灵草丛后面，手里攥着一根萝卜。最里头那株紫玉参旁边，「咔、咔」两声。
setup.en: The tenth of the tenth month, midnight, the herb garden. You squat downwind behind a clump of herbs, a radish in your fist. By the purple jade ginseng at the far end: crack, crack.

recap.zh: 药园偷草的，是一只狰。它扑过来试你；你没下死手，放下一根萝卜。它吃了萝卜，在你脚边团成一团睡着了——小狰跟了你。
recap.en: The herb thief was a zheng. It came at you to try you; you didn't strike to kill, and laid down a radish. It ate the radish and curled up asleep at your feet — Little Zheng is yours.

zh: 五条尾巴，一只独角，一身赤红的毛。
偷来的，怎么吃都吃不饱；给的，一根就饱了。
en: The tenth of the tenth month, midnight, the herb garden.
Five tails, one horn, fur blazing red.
Stolen, never full; given, one is enough.

label.en: Open your hands, and set down the radish

exits.means: weathers the zheng's test without striking to kill, then gives it the radish; it joins him

withdrawn.zh: 小狰「咔、咔」两声，窜回了灵草丛里，又探出一只独角来。——再来。
withdrawn.en: Little Zheng goes crack, crack, darts back into the herbs, and pokes its one horn out again. — Again.

what.zh: 十月初八，周衡把药园巡夜交给了你；工钱是四分之一根蜡烛，和一句「记账」。
what.en: The eighth of the tenth month, Zhou Heng handed you the herb-garden night watch; the pay was a quarter candle and "on the books."

story.zh:
它扒拉到第二株，停了下来，鼻子朝西边抽了两抽。风打了个转，它闻着了。它盯着他藏身的那丛灵草，身子往下一伏，五条尾巴一齐竖了起来，嘴里「咔、咔、咔」地响，又急又硬。小满心口跟着一紧，便让肚子一落，落得长长的，把那一紧按了下去，这才慢慢地站起身来，两只手摊开，让它瞧见他手里什么也没有——除了一根萝卜。他走了三步，弯下腰，把萝卜轻轻放在它面前的地上，退了回去，又蹲下了。

它停下嘴，看了看萝卜，又看了看他。那个眼神，小满到老都记得：头一层是「你在侮辱谁？」，第二层是「本兽吃的是灵草」，第三层——第三层他当时没看懂，后来才懂了，那一层是：「……这是给我的？」它盯着萝卜看了很久很久。然后，它把萝卜吃了。

它吃萝卜，跟吃灵草不一样。吃灵草，它是抱着啃，啃一口，四下里张望一眼，像怕人抢；吃萝卜，它是趴在地上，两只前爪按着，一口一口，吃得很慢，连萝卜缨子都吃了。吃完了，打了个又长又响的嗝，就地一歪，五条尾巴把自己团团围住，睡着了——没跑，当着一个生人的面。

小满蹲在那里，一动也不敢动。这东西偷了一年的灵草，越偷越饿；一根萝卜，不值一文钱，是人家给它的，它倒吃饱了。他想起了马小宝睡着了还在食盒里摸的那一只手，心口有一点发凉。
story.en:
Pawing at a second herb, it stopped and twitched its nose westward twice. The wind had turned; it had caught him. It stared at the clump he was hiding behind, crouched low, all five tails standing up, its mouth going *ke, ke, ke*, fast and hard. Xiaoman's heart tightened; he let his belly drop, a long, long drop, and pressed the tightness down, then slowly stood up, hands open, so it could see there was nothing in them — except a radish. He walked three steps, bent, set the radish gently on the ground in front of it, stepped back, and squatted again.

It stopped eating, looked at the radish, then at him. That look Xiaoman remembered into old age: the first layer said "Who do you think you're insulting?"; the second, "I eat spirit herbs"; the third — the third he didn't understand then, only later; it said: "…This is for me?" It stared at the radish a long, long time. Then it ate the radish.

It ate the radish differently from the herbs. Herbs it hugged and gnawed, a bite, then a look all round, as if afraid someone would snatch it; the radish it ate lying down, both forepaws holding it, bite by bite, very slowly, leaves and all. When it finished it gave a long, loud burp, flopped over where it was, wrapped its five tails round itself, and fell asleep — didn't run, in front of a stranger.

Xiaoman squatted there and didn't dare move. The thing had stolen herbs for a year and grown hungrier the more it stole; a radish, not worth a copper, given to it by somebody, and it was full. He thought of Ma Xiaobao's hand, still groping in the food box in his sleep, and his heart went a little cold.

story.zh:
萝卜是从伙房讨来的。小满傍晚去帮厨，削了一下午的萝卜，削完了，捧着一根，老老实实地对胖大娘道：「大娘，我想要一根萝卜。」胖大娘瞧了瞧他：「要萝卜干什么？」小满道：「练功。」胖大娘脸上的肉一抽一抽的，从筐里又拣了一根最大的，一齐塞进他怀里：「两根。练两遍。」

子时，药园。药园在后山的半腰上，三面是崖，一面是那道矮矮的石墙。园子里一畦一畦的灵草，叶子在夜里泛着一点幽幽的光，像一园子没点着的灯笼。小满吸了一口气——那口气里的米粒，比他想的还要稠。他正要闭上眼睛，墙外头亮起了一盏灯笼。

灯笼后头是马小宝，身后跟着两个跟班，一人一只食盒。马小宝在墙头上嚷道：「沈师弟！师兄来陪你巡夜！」三个人翻了进来，在园子门口的石阶上一坐，灯笼往中间一搁，食盒一开，桂花糕的甜香、腌肉的咸香，顺着风，飘了满园子。小满道：「小宝哥，巡夜要静。」马小宝道：「静什么？贼听见有人，就不敢来了。这叫——打草惊蛇。」三个人吃了半夜，笑了半夜，丑时一过，拍拍屁股走了，灯笼和一只空食盒丢在石阶上，谁也没想起来拿。

天快亮的时候，小满把园子一处一处看过去，看到最西头，一株灵草，齐根没了。

那天上午，周衡在页脚那一道底下，又画了一道。小满回到药园，蹲在那株灵草的断茬跟前。他爹不识字，可他认得山里每一种蹄印爪印。茬口齐齐的，是一口咬断的，那东西牙口好。泥地上几个小小的爪印，猫儿大小，却比猫爪深，那东西身子沉。爪印边上，泥地上扫出一片扇形的印子，一道一道的，数一数，五道。一条尾巴扫不出五道来，除非是五条尾巴。墙角的石头上，还挂着一撮毛，赤红赤红，比马小宝那件狐皮袄还红。

爪印是从西头的崖根底下来的，又回崖根底下去。昨夜那盏灯笼搁在东头，风从东边来，桂花糕、腌肉、三个人的汗味，一股脑儿顺着风往西边飘。那东西闻得见人，便绕到没人的那一头，吃了就走。先看风，后看鹿。他爹的话，一句顶一句用。

第二夜，小满把马家丢下的那盏灯笼点上，连那只还剩着糕渣的食盒，一并搁在园子东头，自己绕到西头，在崖根底下风往园里灌的地方，一丛半人高的灵草后面蹲了下来。东头有灯、有糕味，那东西今夜只会往没人的西头来——往他怀里来。他手里攥着一根萝卜，一动不动地蹲着，像老松底下那一截树桩子。用志不分。天地再大，他只认得脸上的风。

丑时过了一半，药园最里头，那株最值钱的「紫玉参」旁边，蹲着一个东西。猫儿大小，一身赤红的毛，给灵草叶子那点幽光一映，红得发亮，身后拖着五条尾巴；头上生一只独角，短短的，尖尖的，像一截没长成的笋。它两只前爪抱着一株灵草，吃得咔嚓咔嚓直响，一边吃，一边「咔、咔」地叫，像是有人拿两块小石头在对着敲。木牌极轻地暖了一下，一个困得几乎听不清的声音，嫌弃地道：「……章莪之山的狰。五尾一角，其音如击石。《山海经》上都有……你们凡人，不念书的么……」
story.en:
The radish came from the kitchen. Xiaoman went to help there towards evening and peeled radishes all afternoon; when he'd finished he held one up and said honestly to the fat auntie: "Auntie, I'd like a radish." She looked him over. "What do you want a radish for?" "Practice," said Xiaoman. The flesh of her face twitched; she picked the biggest one out of the basket and pushed both into his coat. "Two. Practise twice."

Midnight. The herb garden. It lay halfway up the back mountain, cliffs on three sides and on the fourth that low stone wall. Inside, bed after bed of spirit herbs, their leaves giving off a faint glow at night, like a garden of unlit lanterns. Xiaoman drew a breath — there were more grains of rice in it than he'd imagined. He was about to close his eyes when a lantern lit up beyond the wall.

Behind the lantern was Ma Xiaobao, with two followers, each carrying a food box. From the top of the wall Ma Xiaobao shouted, "Brother Shen! Your senior's come to keep you company on watch!" The three of them climbed in and sat on the steps by the garden gate, the lantern between them, the boxes open, and the sweet smell of osmanthus cake and the salt smell of cured meat drifted all over the garden on the wind. Xiaoman said, "Brother Xiaobao, a night watch should be quiet." Ma Xiaobao said, "Quiet what? If the thief hears people, he won't dare come. That's called — beating the grass to scare the snake." The three of them ate half the night and laughed half the night, and after the hour of Chou slapped their backsides and left, the lantern and an empty food box forgotten on the steps.

Towards dawn Xiaoman went over the garden bit by bit, and at the far west end: one herb, gone, bitten off at the root.

That morning Zhou Heng drew another line under the line at the foot of the page. Xiaoman went back to the garden and squatted by the herb's stump. His father couldn't read, but he could read every hoofprint and paw print in the mountains. The cut was clean — bitten through in one go; the thing had good teeth. In the mud were a few small paw prints, cat-sized but deeper than a cat's; the thing was heavy. Beside the prints the mud was swept into a fan of marks, stroke after stroke — he counted: five. One tail can't sweep five strokes, unless it's five tails. And on a stone in the corner hung a tuft of fur, red, blood red, redder than Ma Xiaobao's fox-fur jacket.

The prints came from the foot of the cliff at the west end and went back there. Last night the lantern had stood at the east end, the wind came from the east, and osmanthus cake, cured meat and three boys' sweat all drifted west on it. The thing could smell people, so it went round to the end with nobody and ate and left. Watch the wind first, then the deer. His father's sayings were good for one thing after another.

The second night Xiaoman lit the lantern the Mas had left behind and set it, with the food box that still had cake crumbs in it, at the east end of the garden; he himself went round to the west end, to the foot of the cliff where the wind poured into the garden, and squatted behind a clump of herbs half a man high. Light and cake-smell in the east — tonight the thing would come only to the empty west end, straight into his arms. He held a radish in his hand and squatted without moving, like the stump of a tree under the old pine. The will undivided. However big heaven and earth, all he knew was the wind on his face.

Halfway through the hour of Chou, deep in the garden, beside the most precious "purple jade ginseng", something crouched. Cat-sized, all over red fur that shone in the faint glow of the leaves, five tails trailing behind; on its head a single horn, short and sharp, like a bamboo shoot that hadn't grown up. It hugged an herb in its two forepaws and crunched away, and as it ate it went *ke, ke*, like someone knocking two pebbles together. The token warmed very faintly, and a voice so sleepy he could hardly hear it said, disgusted: "…A zheng from Mount Zhang'e. Five tails, one horn, its voice like struck stone. It's in the *Classic of Mountains and Seas*… don't you mortals read…"
